paper_or_case_title: Insulin-induced Drosophila S6 kinase activation requires phosphoinositide 3-kinase and protein kinase B
organism_context: Drosophila melanogaster Kc167 and S2 cells
reported_issue: Retraction lists cross-figure reuse involving dPKB, including Fig. 1B dPKB appearing as part of Fig. 7A dS6K, Fig. 2B dS6K appearing as Fig. 2B dPKB after horizontal transformation, Kc167 dS6K appearing as S2 dPKB after horizontal transformation, and Kc167 p-dPKB appearing in part as S2 p-dPKB after horizontal transformation.
results_sentence: A 2025 Biochemical Journal retraction documents multiple transformed or reused Drosophila dPKB Western-blot images, providing a direct audit precedent around the approximately 60 kDa Akt neighborhood.
species_interpretation: direct D. melanogaster cell-line case; 59.9 kDa is the current FlyBase predicted mass for the common 530-aa Akt isoforms; the retraction itself does not adjudicate research misconduct

paper_or_case_title: Insulin-induced Drosophila S6 kinase activation requires phosphoinositide 3-kinase and protein kinase B
organism_context: Drosophila melanogaster Kc167 and S2 cells
reported_issue: Retraction lists several dS6K similarities: Fig. 1B dPKB appears as part of Fig. 7A dS6K; Fig. 2B dS6K appears as Fig. 2B dPKB with horizontal transformation; Fig. 4A Kc167 dS6K appears in part as S2 dPKB with horizontal transformation; and Fig. 4B Kc167 dS6K appears as S2 dS6K with horizontal transformation.
results_sentence: The same retraction documents repeated or horizontally transformed dS6K Western-blot material across figures and protein labels, providing a direct Drosophila audit precedent in the current-reference approximately 55 kDa S6k neighborhood.
species_interpretation: direct D. melanogaster cell-line case; 55.4 kDa is the current FlyBase predicted mass for S6k-PA/PB. FlyBase also records older historical 637-aa annotations with predicted masses around 73-76 kDa, so the atlas should retain this historical-annotation caveat

paper_or_case_title: Drosophila Dullard functions as a Mad phosphatase to terminate BMP signaling
reported_issue: Scientific Reports correction states that the pMadS212 blot in Fig. 4c was unintentionally swapped with the pMadCter blot from Fig. 4d.
results_sentence: A publisher correction documents an identity swap between two phospho-Mad Western blots in Drosophila cells, mapping the protein-level audit precedent to the approximately 50.5 kDa Mad-PA neighborhood.
species_interpretation: direct D. melanogaster correction; 50.5 kDa is the current FlyBase predicted mass for Mad-PA; this is a corrected assembly/identity error, not a misconduct finding

paper_or_case_title: Drosophila Dullard functions as a Mad phosphatase to terminate BMP signaling
reported_issue: Scientific Reports correction states that Flag-Mad-AVA blots were unintentionally swapped between Supplementary Fig. 2c and 2d.
results_sentence: The same correction documents swapped Flag-Mad-AVA blots between supplementary panels, providing a direct Drosophila blot-identity audit precedent around the Mad molecular-weight neighborhood.
species_interpretation: direct D. melanogaster correction; 50.5 kDa is the current FlyBase core Mad-PA mass and does not include the small FLAG tag; tagged construct may migrate slightly higher

paper_or_case_title: DNMT3L enables accumulation and inheritance of epimutations in transgenic Drosophila
reported_issue: Scientific Reports author correction states that the H3K9me3 Western-blot example was captured in the wrong orientation and displayed at 180-degree rotation; a biological replicate replaced the panel. The correction also explains that similarity between H3K9me3 and H3 blots arose from stripping and reprobing.
results_sentence: A Drosophila author correction documents a 180-degree orientation error in an H3K9me3 Western blot, supplying a lower-severity presentation-integrity precedent in the approximately 15.4 kDa histone H3 neighborhood.
species_interpretation: direct D. melanogaster correction; 15.4 kDa is the current FlyBase predicted mass for canonical histone H3 copies; this is a corrected presentation error and should not be described as misconduct or fabrication
